task_summary: Implement a HomePage component in React 18 + TypeScript that renders a "Quick Start" table (rows derived from ToolDef via mapping functions) and a circular closed-loop SVG diagram (nodes positioned via computeNodePosition). The component must integrate with Convex for real-time data, use Tailwind CSS v3 for styling, and follow the project's strict TypeScript/React conventions.

findings.finding: computeNodePosition should use standard parametric circle equations: x = centerX + radius * cos(2π * step / totalNodes - π/2), y = centerY + radius * sin(2π * step / totalNodes - π/2). The -π/2 offset starts placement at 12 o'clock. This is the canonical approach for placing N nodes evenly around a circle. Edge case: totalNodes=0 must be guarded against (division by zero). For totalNodes=1, the single node sits at the top.
findings.source: Standard computational geometry / D3.js circular layout patterns
findings.relevance: Directly implements computeNodePosition and drives ClosedLoopDiagram rendering

findings.finding: Use a fixed viewBox (e.g., '0 0 400 400') on the SVG element and let CSS (width: 100%, height: auto) handle responsive scaling. This decouples layout math from viewport size. The SVGViewBoxSpec type should encode minX, minY, width, height. Avoid hardcoding pixel widths on the SVG element itself — Tailwind's w-full + aspect-square or explicit max-w-* classes are preferred.
findings.source: MDN SVG viewBox documentation; React SVG best practices
findings.relevance: ClosedLoopDiagram must render correctly across screen sizes without layout breakage

findings.finding: To draw a closed loop connecting nodes in order, iterate through the DiagramNodeList and draw <line> or <path> elements from node[i] to node[(i+1) % length]. Using SVG <path> with 'd' attribute and cubic bezier curves gives smoother results, but straight <line> elements are simpler and sufficient for a diagram. Add arrowhead markers via <defs><marker> for directional indication.
findings.source: SVG specification; common React diagramming patterns
findings.relevance: Core visual requirement of ClosedLoopDiagram — nodes connected in a cycle

findings.finding: Use useQuery from 'convex/react' to fetch tool definitions reactively. The hook returns undefined while loading and the typed result once available. Always handle the undefined/loading state explicitly — render a skeleton or spinner. Do NOT use useEffect + fetch; Convex hooks manage subscriptions automatically. If tool data is static (no Convex query needed), import it directly from the tool_data dependency module.
findings.source: Convex React documentation; project dependency list includes 'tool_data'
findings.relevance: HomePage needs ToolDefList data; the dependency on 'tool_data' suggests it may be a static module rather than a Convex query, but the pattern should handle both

findings.finding: toQuickStartRow, toDiagramNode, and their list variants (toQuickStartRows, toDiagramNodes) should be pure functions with no side effects. The list variants should simply be tools.map(toQuickStartRow) and tools.map(toDiagramNode) respectively. Keep these in a separate utility file or co-located with the HomePage if short. Type the return values explicitly per project standards.
findings.source: Functional programming patterns in React/TypeScript codebases
findings.relevance: Ensures testability, composability, and compliance with the project's type annotation requirements

findings.finding: Project mandates <300 lines per file. HomePage should be the orchestrating component that imports ClosedLoopDiagram and a QuickStartTable (or inline table). ClosedLoopDiagram should be its own file. Mapping/utility functions should be in a separate utils file. Estimated breakdown: HomePage (~80-120 lines), ClosedLoopDiagram (~80-120 lines), mappers/utils (~40-60 lines), types (~30-50 lines from type_registry).
findings.source: Project Operating Procedures (file size limit, component splitting preference)

findings.topic: React Key Props for Dynamic Lists
findings.finding: When rendering QuickStartRows in a table and DiagramNodes in SVG, each must have a stable, unique key. Use ToolSlug (enum) as the key since it's unique per tool. Avoid using array index as key — if tool order changes, React will mis-reconcile DOM nodes.
findings.relevance: Common pitfall in list rendering; ToolSlug enum provides a natural stable key

findings.finding: SVG <text> elements for node labels should use text-anchor='middle' and dominant-baseline='central' for centering. For accessibility, add <title> and <desc> elements inside the SVG, and role='img' + aria-label on the SVG element. Tailwind classes don't apply inside SVG — use inline SVG attributes or a small set of allowed CSS properties.
findings.source: WAI-ARIA SVG accessibility guidelines; SVG text rendering specs
findings.relevance: ClosedLoopDiagram nodes need labels; accessibility is a professional standard

findings.finding: Use Tailwind utility classes for the QuickStart table: 'table-auto w-full', 'border-collapse', cell padding via 'px-4 py-2', striped rows via 'even:bg-gray-50'. Avoid <table> for layout — only for tabular data (which QuickStartRows are). Use semantic <thead>, <tbody>, <th scope="col"> elements.
findings.source: Tailwind CSS v3 documentation; HTML table accessibility guidelines
findings.relevance: QuickStartRowList renders as a data table on the HomePage

findings.finding: If ToolDefList is stable (static import or Convex-cached), memoization is unnecessary. If it could change frequently, wrap toQuickStartRows and toDiagramNodes calls in useMemo with [tools] as dependency. computeNodePosition is a pure math function — no memoization needed unless called in a hot loop with identical arguments. Premature optimization is unlikely needed here.
findings.source: React useMemo documentation; performance profiling best practices
findings.relevance: Ensures smooth rendering if tool data updates in real-time via Convex subscriptions

findings.finding: Handle the case where ToolDefList is empty: QuickStart table should show a meaningful empty state (e.g., 'No tools configured'), and ClosedLoopDiagram should either render nothing or a placeholder. computeNodePosition with totalNodes=0 must not crash.
findings.relevance: Frequently missed edge case in data-driven UIs

findings.finding: HomePage must be registered as a route element in the app's router configuration (e.g., path='/' element={<HomePage />}). Per project rules, all pages must be reachable via React Router routes. If tool items link to detail pages, use <Link to={`/tools/${slug}`}> from react-router-dom, not <a href>.
findings.source: React Router v6 documentation; project verification requirements
findings.relevance: Project mandates all pages reachable via routes; HomePage is likely the index route

recommended_approach:
**File Structure:**
1. `src/components/HomePage/index.tsx` — HomePage component (~100 lines). Imports tool data, calls mapping functions, renders QuickStart table + ClosedLoopDiagram.
2. `src/components/HomePage/ClosedLoopDiagram.tsx` — SVG diagram component (~100 lines). Receives DiagramNodeList via props, calls computeNodePosition for each node, renders nodes as circles with labels connected by lines/arrows in a closed loop.
3. `src/components/HomePage/utils.ts` — Pure mapping functions: toQuickStartRow, toDiagramNode, toQuickStartRows, toDiagramNodes, computeNodePosition (~60 lines).
4. Types come from the `type_registry` dependency.

**Algorithm for ClosedLoopDiagram:**
- Define a viewBox (e.g., `0 0 500 500`) with center at (250, 250) and radius ~180.
- For each node at index `i` of `totalNodes`, call `computeNodePosition(i, totalNodes, 250, 250, 180)`.
- Render SVG `<circle>` + `<text>` at each computed (x, y).
- Draw `<line>` or `<path>` from each node to the next, with the last connecting back to the first (closed loop). Use SVG `<marker>` for arrowheads.

**Data Flow:**
- Import `ToolDefList` from `tool_data` module.
- Derive `QuickStartRowList` via `toQuickStartRows(tools)`.
- Derive `DiagramNodeList` via `toDiagramNodes(tools)`.
- Pass `DiagramNodeList` to `ClosedLoopDiagram` as a typed prop.

**Key Guards:**
- Empty list → render empty state for both table and diagram.
- `computeNodePosition` guards `totalNodes === 0` → returns center point.
- All exported functions and components have explicit TypeScript type annotations.
- Use ToolSlug as React key for list items.
- SVG has `role="img"` and `aria-label` for accessibility.
alternatives_considered: Using a third-party diagramming library (e.g., react-flow, d3-force) for ClosedLoopDiagram — rejected because the layout is a simple circular arrangement of known nodes, not a dynamic graph. A library would add unnecessary bundle weight and complexity.

Using CSS Grid or Flexbox for circular layout instead of SVG — rejected because CSS-based circular layouts require absolute positioning hacks and don't support connector lines natively. SVG is the correct tool for this diagram.

Rendering the QuickStart section as cards instead of a table — viable UX alternative, but the type system defines QuickStartRow (tabular semantics) and QuickStartRowList, strongly suggesting a table presentation.

Fetching tool data via Convex useQuery vs. static import from tool_data module — the dependency list includes 'tool_data' as a module, suggesting static data. If tools are stored in Convex DB, the pattern would shift to useQuery. Recommend starting with static import and migrating to Convex query if needed.
Co-locating all functions in HomePage.tsx vs. splitting into separate files — splitting is preferred given the 300-line limit and the number of functions (7 functions + 2 components).
risks: Type definitions in type_registry may not match assumptions about field names (e.g., QuickStartRow fields, DiagramNode fields). Must inspect actual type_registry before implementation.
tool_data module structure is unknown — it may export a raw array, a function, or a Convex query reference. Implementation must adapt to actual export shape.
SVG text sizing and node circle radius may need tuning depending on label length. Long tool names could overflow node boundaries — consider text truncation or dynamic font sizing.
ClosedLoopDiagram connector lines may overlap node circles if radius or node sizing isn't calibrated. Need to compute line start/end points at circle edges rather than center-to-center.
If ToolDefList grows beyond ~12 items, circular layout becomes crowded and labels overlap. Should consider limiting displayed nodes or switching to an alternative layout at higher counts.
HexColor type suggests nodes have configurable colors — must ensure sufficient contrast against the background for accessibility (WCAG AA minimum 4.5:1 ratio).
compliance_notes: All exported functions must have explicit TypeScript return type annotations per project standards.
React functional components only — no class components.
Props typed via TypeScript interfaces (e.g., ClosedLoopDiagramProps).
All styling via Tailwind CSS v3 classes — no custom CSS. Exception: inline SVG attributes (fill, stroke, etc.) are acceptable since Tailwind doesn't cover all SVG properties.
File size must stay under 300 lines each — split into 3+ files as recommended.
HomePage must be registered in React Router v6 route configuration and be reachable.
Import Convex hooks from 'convex/react' if real-time data is used.
Dev server port 4000 in vite.config.ts — not directly relevant to this component but must not be disrupted.
All tests must run with vitest — mapping functions and computeNodePosition are highly testable pure functions.
